page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-4 is an x86_64 compute-oriented instance configured with 4 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 2 physical Intel cores via multithreading. It features 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The processor architecture includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates advanced hardware instruction sets, including AVX-512, Intel AMX for matrix operations, and cryptographic extensions such as AES and SHA-NI. The instance is provisioned without local storage or discrete graphics accelerators.

Performance evaluation indicates stable single-threaded throughput, shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 1840.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1577.19. Single-threaded data handling remains balanced, with gzip compression registering 27.98 GB/sec and static web serving throughput reaching 6.82 GB/sec. Conversely, overall multithreaded capacity and memory subsystem speeds are constrained by the physical two-core footprint. PassMark CPU reached 5901.55 and Geekbench multi-core measured 4108.0, while PassMark memory scored 900.02. Memory bandwidth recorded 37.38 GB/sec read and 23.04 GB/sec write on large block transfers.

The n4-highcpu-4 provides dedicated CPU resources without burstable throttling, pairing modest core density with reduced memory allocation. The primary operational tradeoff is limited memory bandwidth and capacity, which prevents effective deployment for large data stores or intensive parallel analysis. It is appropriately configured for compute-bound tasks, continuous integration runners, containerized microservices, and lightweight web serving that require reliable compute execution without large resident memory footprints.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-4 is a compute-focused virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical Intel x86_64 cores and 8.0 GB of system memory. Structured with a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio, the processor architecture incorporates 260 MB of L3 cache along with AVX-512 and Intel AMX instruction sets. The instance includes no bundled local storage drives and zero discrete GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate stable single-core execution, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1840.0 and static web serving throughput of 6.82 GB/sec. Multithreaded and memory subsystem metrics reflect the two-core physical boundary, with PassMark memory scoring 900.02. Given its dedicated core allocation and lower memory capacity, n4-highcpu-4 is best matched with lightweight web serving, stateless microservices, build pipelines, and modest CPU-bound batch tasks.
